svg.text: Vital signs: normal adult ranges and the errors that fake them
SIGN
ADULT NORMAL
WHAT MAKES IT WRONG
Temperature
36.1 to 37.2 degrees C
Hot drink, site, poor contact
Pulse
60 to 100 per minute
Counting 15 s when irregular
Respirations
12 to 20 per minute
Telling the patient you are counting
Blood pressure
below 120 over 80
Wrong cuff size, arm not at heart level
Oxygen saturation
95 to 100 per cent
Cold hands, nail varnish, movement
Blood pressure — the cuff decides the number
Cuff TOO SMALL → reading too HIGH
Cuff TOO LARGE → reading too LOW
Bladder should cover about 80 per cent of
the arm circumference.
Arm BELOW heart level → falsely high
Arm ABOVE heart level → falsely low
Counting respirations — the trick
Breathing is partly under voluntary control.
If the patient knows you are counting,
the rate you measure is not their real rate.
Keep your fingers on the pulse and count
the breaths without saying anything.
Count a full minute if it is irregular.
Postural (orthostatic) hypotension — how to measure it
Lie the patient flat for 5 minutes and record BP and pulse. Stand them, then record again at 1 and 3 minutes.
POSITIVE if systolic falls 20 mmHg or more, or diastolic falls 10 mmHg or more.
A rising pulse with a falling BP suggests volume depletion. Stay with the patient — this is a falls risk.
Common causes: dehydration, bleeding, antihypertensives, diuretics, prolonged bed rest, autonomic neuropathy.
